The answer is C: a tracheostomy is used as an aid to weaning patients from a ventilator, because it reduces dead space and the work of breathing and lets sedation be lightened. The team note is wrong. The tube sits below the vocal cords and bypasses the larynx, so it doesn't restore cord movement or treat paralysed cords. It also isn't a standard aid to swallowing or a routine step before neck surgery.

CONFIDENCE: 90
